correctness.rationale: The semantics-to-matching translation and the row-finite Hall criterion are correct. Kontinen and Ciardelli's semantics for the displayed formula say exactly that a failing subteam is the graph of an injective total map \(f:D\to D\) with non-surjective range. Choosing an omitted right value \(b\) turns this into a system of distinct representatives for the family \(R(a)\setminus\{b\}\). When every row is finite, the infinite Hall theorem for families of finite sets is equivalent to the Hall inequality on every finite left subfamily; negating it gives the stated finite certificate. The boundary example is also correct: all positive left vertices force their own images, leaving no injective image for zero, while every finite left set still satisfies Hall after deleting right value zero. The actual package checker exhaustively compares SDR existence with finite Hall inequalities on all small finite set-families and checks the escaping-witness truncations.

originality.rationale: The audited theorem is a direct composition of two published statements. Kontinen and Ciardelli already unpack the exact formula into functional, injective, total-domain, non-surjective-range conditions, so the first matching statement is only a change of vocabulary. Cameron's current Hall survey states the infinite Hall theorem in precisely the needed form for a family of finite sets: an SDR exists iff every finite subfamily satisfies Hall. Applying it to \(A_a=R(a)\setminus\{b\}\) gives the row-finite certificate in one step. The same survey also recalls the canonical failure when one allowed set is infinite and the remaining sets are forced singletons, which is the same mechanism as the audited boundary example. Accordingly, the final claim is mechanically covered by the exact source semantics plus a standard theorem and its standard boundary example.
